9/11/2017                                                                                           dates



Dear Dr Omar,
Re: Mrs Somarni Khaze                       DOB: 12/04/1971

I am writing to refer Mrs Khaze who has been diagnosed with breast cancer for immediate
surgical intervention if possible.

On 22/10/2017, Mrs Khaze presented with a small left breast lump, not painful and without
nipple discharge. On examination, there was a 2*2 cm hard non-tender left breast lump with ill
defined margins, but not tender. In addition, palpable mobile axillary lymph nodes were
presented. The right breast was normal except for a scar from a previous surgery. Therefore,        Comment [OET2]: noted
ultrasound and mammogram were requested.

On 6/11/2017, Mrs Khaze was anxious and worried about the results of the investigations. The
ultrasound showed 18*16 mm nodule in the left breast with variable echogenicity and the
mammogram revealed a highly suspicious area of malignancy in the left breast with multiple
nodules in the axilla. So, core biopsy was ordered.                                                 Comment [OET3]: Therefore,: so is informal

Today, the biopsy result showed a moderately differentiated invasive ductal carcinoma in the left
breast.

It is worth mentioning that Mrs Khaze has a history of benign lump in the right breast which was    Comment [OET4]: had
successfully resected and her sister also had a history of breast cancer.                           Comment [OET5]: has: use present simple
                                                                                                    for facts
It would be great if you could operate on her and answer her inquires about the possibility of
immediate reconstructive surgery.

Please, if you have any questions, do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor Tin Aung
